Armstrong 1808 shorthand

Armstrong to Madison, Paris, 20 Feb 1808 (NARA RG 59 M34 roll 14, frames 0030-0032): every ink component of the 28 shorthand-bearing lines, cut automatically. The tiles start in 36 provisional shape piles made by a script (k-means on stroke shape, h74/piles.py): a pile is named T<number> where its typical tile sits close to that shape on Tomokiyo's 38-type sheet (tomokiyo_38_types.png beside this page, h59/person_pack/), otherwise s<number>. These are starting guesses for you to correct, not readings. Take out what does not belong and re-home it; rename a pile to its Tomokiyo number when you see it; put numerals in a pile called digits, dots and ticks in ASIDE unless they belong to a sign, and mark a tile that joins two signs or splits one as BAD-CUT. Shape only: nothing here asks for a reading.

Step 1 · Clean each pileLook along a pile. Tap any sign that is not like the others: it moves to the "Taken out" tray at the bottom. Tap it there to put it back. When a pile looks right, press "This pile is done".
See a sign largerPress and hold a sign (or press "View larger" on a pile): it opens on its line, the sign in brackets, with Next and Previous.
Step 2 · Place the taken-out signsEach taken-out sign is shown large with every other pile below it, closest-looking first. Drag it onto its pile, or just tap the pile. "None of these: new sign" starts a new pile; nothing to type.
